concepts.name: Indigo fermentation vat readiness by flower/color/smell
concepts.open_problem: A fermentation indigo vat is judged 'ready/working' by a triad of sensory cues - the blue surface 'flower' (foam of trapped indigo), the yellow-green reduced liquor color, and the distinct bacterial-fermentation odor - rather than by instruments; reading these to decide when to dye and when the vat is alive is tacit and bacteria-dependent.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no consumer app judges indigo vat readiness; only recipe blogs and a microbiota study)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The color, the foam, the smell indicate whether the chemistry is working.

concepts.name: Natural dye-bath exhaustion judgment by color
concepts.open_problem: Dyers reuse a bath for successive 'exhaust' batches and must judge by eye when residual color has dropped enough (and that some dyes like catechu barely exhaust) to predict the paler shade the next fiber will take; this remaining-strength estimate by appearance is experiential and material-specific.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no shipping app estimates dye-bath exhaustion; only craft blogs)
concepts.verbatim_quote: After removing the first batch of fiber, a dye bath typically still contains 30-60% of its original color concentration, and eventually the bath becomes exhausted when no more color transfers.

concepts.name: Vegetable-tanning endpoint judged by sight and feel
concepts.open_problem: In traditional veg tanneries, the condition of hides and tan liquors and the completion of tannage are judged by experienced workers through sight and hand-feel (firmness, grain response, even a flex 'creak'), not automated sensors; knowing when leather has fully struck through is an embodied judgment.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no app judges tanning endpoint; results were craft/retail guides)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Experienced workers in vegetable tanneries can judge the condition of hides and tanning baths by sight and feel, which keeps the process rooted in human expertise instead of automated systems.

concepts.name: Judging yarn twist / balance by hand (plyback feel)
concepts.open_problem: How much twist 'is enough' for a given fiber is decided by hand - via plyback samples, letting a skein dangle to see if it kinks, and even hearing/feeling the fibers slide - a perceptual, fiber-specific judgment that resists explicit rules despite patents for instrument twist-measurement.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (industrial twist-measurement patents exist as hardware; no consumer app judges handspun twist by feel)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Only skill and experience can tell us how much twist is enough for a particular fiber.

concepts.name: Judging felting/fulling completion by firmness not size
concepts.open_problem: Wet-felters decide a piece is done by real-time tactile feedback - firmness, stability, absence of loose fibers via the pinch test - and control the 'shock' to the fibers by hand, rather than by reaching a target dimension; the stop-point is a felt judgment, not a measurement.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (shrinkage 'calculators' exist but only do arithmetic on a measured sample; no app judges fulling completion)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Rather than relying on dimensions alone, stop felting based on firmness and stability, not just dimensions.

concepts.name: Fleece grading/sorting by hand-feel (wool classing)
concepts.open_problem: Traditional wool classers grade and sort fleeces by trained hand-feel and eye - fineness, staple length/strength, crimp - without instruments, separating qualities within a single fleece that only the hand can distinguish; British Wool says it takes ~3 years to qualify.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (objective-measurement instruments and AI fibre-science research exist, but no consumer app replaces the hand-classer's tactile grading)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Traditional subjective systems for wool classing rely on the trained judgment of experienced classers to assess fiber characteristics through visual inspection, hand feel, and tactile evaluation, without the use of measurement instruments.

concepts.name: Reading the sky / clouds for tomorrow's weather (weather lore)
concepts.open_problem: Folk forecasting reads sky color (red sky rules), cloud type/sequence and movement over time to anticipate weather; the skill is in integrating evolving cues over days, but the underlying nowcasting task is now heavily served by consumer apps.
concepts.app_market_check: app-saturated - consumer AI weather/nowcasting apps ship widely (Rainbow Weather AI nowcasting, Google WeatherNext in Pixel Weather/Search, AccuWeather, Atmo); the practical 'what's the weather' task is covered
concepts.verbatim_quote: Rainbow Weather delivers hyper-accurate minute-by-minute forecasts powered by AI and machine learning, with a unique nowcasting engine that predicts precipitation up to 4 hours in advance.

concepts.name: Cloud-type reading skill (perceptual, ongoing observation)
concepts.open_problem: Predicting weather from clouds is a centuries-old perceptual skill with modest (~60-75%) accuracy that requires sustained observation of cloud change and motion, not single-snapshot ID; the human reading-of-the-sky-over-time is distinct from app point-forecasts, though apps dominate the end goal.
concepts.app_market_check: partly app-covered - cloud/radar apps (e.g. RainViewer) and AI forecasters serve the prediction goal; less so the embodied 'watch the sky evolve' skill itself
concepts.verbatim_quote: Observing cloud types as a means to predict the weather yields an accuracy of 60–75 percent.

concepts.name: Phenological folk indicators for planting/foraging timing
concepts.open_problem: Traditional practice times planting and wild-harvest by biological cues (lilac bloom -> beans, forsythia -> peas, dogwood bloom end -> stop hunting morels); knowing which local indicator predicts the right window is place-specific traditional knowledge tying plant phenology to soil/temperature readiness.
concepts.app_market_check: partial - citizen-science phenology platforms (USA-NPN Nature's Notebook) and agritech microclimate apps (Sencrop) record/forecast phenology, but the folk indicator->action mapping is not packaged as a consumer app
concepts.verbatim_quote: Examples include planting when the spring peepers begin peeping; treating the lawn for crabgrass when the forsythia is blooming; and ending the hunt for morel mushrooms once the dogwoods stop blooming.

concepts.name: Distinguishing edible vs toxic wild mushrooms (spore/smell/substrate)
concepts.open_problem: Safe ID hinges on hard-to-photograph cues - spore-print color, odor, bruising, substrate - because deadly look-alikes grow alongside edibles; this is a high-stakes multisensory judgment, and notably the AI apps that DO ship are unreliable for the toxic-discrimination part.
concepts.app_market_check: app-saturated but UNSAFE - many mushroom-ID apps ship (Picture Mushroom, Mushroom Identificator, iNaturalist) yet top app scored only ~49% and look-alikes to deadly Amanita/Galerina were misidentified >30% of the time; apps exist but do not solve the safety-critical judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: Most AI-based apps can't take into account the factors crucial to identifying a mushroom with confidence, like the mushroom's substrate, bruising features, and smell.

notes: Least AI-touched / most fertile tacit judgments with NO shipping consumer app: indigo fermentation-vat readiness by flower+color+smell (none), vegetable-tanning endpoint by sight/feel (none), felting/fulling completion by firmness/pinch-test (none), natural dye-bath exhaustion by color (very-low), judging handspun yarn twist/balance by hand (very-low) - these are the white-space craft gaps. App-saturated tasks per the session-1 lesson: general WEATHER FORECASTING is high AI penetration - consumer AI nowcasting apps (Rainbow Weather, Google WeatherNext, AccuWeather, Atmo) clearly ship and cover the 'what's the weather' goal, so folk sky-reading rated high; cloud-reading rated moderate (radar/forecast apps cover the goal even if the embodied skill differs). MUSHROOM-ID is a nuance: apps DO ship and are widely used (Picture Mushroom, iNaturalist, Mushroom Identificator) so it is NOT visual-ID white space, BUT documented accuracy is poor (~49% best app; >30% miss on deadly Amanita/Galerina look-alikes) and they ignore spore/smell/substrate/bruising - rated high for app presence while flagging the safety-critical sub-judgment as genuinely unsolved. Wool classing (low) and phenology indicators (low) sit in between: instruments/citizen-science/agritech touch them but no consumer app packages the hand-classer's tactile grade or the folk indicator->planting-action mapping.
